bugs.what: The Hunter's Sortie ('Three wolves: the charcoal ring... the leaning stones and clawed trunks north of it') never marks done even after its apparent resolution: I killed the aggressive lean wolf at the charcoal ring and showed the hunter its pelt ('That's the one that jumped anyone who came near the old fire ring... Wood's quieter for it' - reward given), and peacefully avoided the other two via the game's own '(free)' leave-be option per Lys's advice. The quest stayed listed, unresolved, in every status check through turn 628.
bugs.where: Hunter's Camp (west of Last Light) / quest log

bugs.what: The Old Dams quest is introduced at the Meres' South Shore naming three deciders by name - 'Corliss, Yarrow, and Hodd each want a say' - but Corliss's location is never given by any dialogue, room description, or the region's own 'get your bearings' tool. Yarrow (lantern tower) and Hodd (charge barge) were both easy to find; after visiting effectively every landmark in Lantern Holm and the surrounding reed-channels, Corliss never appeared, and the quest was left permanently open.
bugs.where: The South Shore, the Meres / The Old Dams quest

bugs.what: The Warden-marked entry 'press him plainly, watch to watch' (talking to the Free Companies' paymaster) produces only a flavor rebuff - 'He goes flat... Ask your chest business elsewhere' - with no xp tag, no standing change, and no state change of any kind. Every other Warden entry I tried (about a dozen, across all four holds visited) changed something; this one was pure dead air, and I had to fall back on the ordinary will-check option to actually make progress with him.
bugs.where: The Paymaster's Chest-Room, Pennywell / talk to Dray

bugs.what: The two relic dies recovered for Pennywell's coin-rite (Sarel's reverse die, Slade's obverse die) stay in the carried-items list unchanged - 'wants the obverse to be struck true', 'silver-black with age' - even after the town's press is reported striking 'an old king's face now.' It's never said whether the actual relics were used or the new press just adopted the old style; the items are never consumed or referenced again once the bargain resolves, so a player is left guessing what physically happened to them.
bugs.where: The Vault-Door, Pennywell / after 'tell her the vault stays sealed'

bugs.what: Companion-mediation 'call it a draw between them' is a will-check coin flip (roughly 50-65% by my rolls) that, on a miss, costs standing with BOTH quarreling companions equally - observed at both the barrow-doors dispute (Osk/Tamsin, both -1) and the Drowned-Hall covenant dispute (Lys/Osk, both -1). There is no lower-stakes 'just listen, take no side' option distinct from this persuasion attempt, so trying to stay neutral always risks souring both relationships at once.
bugs.where: The Empty Seat (Vale barrow) and the Drowned Hall covenant chamber (Meres) / speak with the company

bugs.what: Crossing from the Meres into Pennywell is never an explicit action even though a 'flat-bottomed ferry sits chained to a post' is described at both landing tiles - the crossing itself is just ordinary 'go east' movement, with no 'board/ride the ferry' verb ever offered. The promised ferry plays as scenery, not an event.
bugs.where: The Far Bank Ferry-Landing / Ferry Cut, the Meres-Pennywell border

bugs.what: Travel-menu categories (e.g. 'toward the Meres', 'toward Pennywell') sometimes omit a landmark clearly stood on and central to the route - 'The Far Bank' (the literal Meres/Pennywell crossing tile) never appears under either region's travel list; you have to route via 'the Far Bank ferry' instead, a differently-named landmark filed under Pennywell.
bugs.where: Any 'travel to a known place' menu near the Meres/Pennywell border

bugs.what: Several wits/grace checks with identical odds needed 2-3 retries before succeeding with no new information or changed circumstance offered between attempts (e.g. the wind-carving check at the Old Watchtower failed twice before succeeding on a nat 20; the water-verse check at the Sunken Shrine failed twice before succeeding). Clearly signposted as retryable, but it reads oddly that persistence alone - not a new approach - is what works.
bugs.where: Old Watchtower and Sunken Shrine, the Vale of Ash

bugs.what: Once the Regent tries to reopen the vault (the 'Pennywell, After' beat), choosing to keep it sealed 'whatever it costs' resolves in a single line with Averil and no return trip, garrison, or lasting threat state - the promised standing cost is real (Crown -1) but the scene itself is one exchange, so the 'cost' feels abstract rather than something you have to weather.
bugs.where: The Counting-House, Pennywell / 'keep it sealed, whatever it costs'

bugs.what: By late-game the carrying-line in every room/status print lists 20+ items, most of them permanent sentimental keepsakes explicitly marked unusable ('a keepsake now, however it came; nothing is owed on it', 'nothing more is owed for it') with no further interaction ever offered - they never clutter a menu, but they do make the inventory line hard to scan for the few items that still matter (the two dies, the covenant stone).
bugs.where: Status/room header 'carrying:' line, from mid-Meres onward

bugs.what: The realm's stated scale - 'the straight road to Marrowgate runs near three hundred turns; a hold seen whole is forty to seventy more, and seeing them all, many times that' - is disclosed only once, buried inside the dense Act 2 status paragraph, never restated or flagged at Act 1's start when a player first commits to the 'see everything' approach.

Fetch/report quests (Perrin's Mother wanting word of her son at Highward/Wardmoor; Two Keepers wanting word of Rowan in Thornwold's Understory) are handed out with no indication of how far those holds are from where the quest is offered - the true distance (dozens to 100+ turns) only becomes apparent from the Act 2 status paragraph's scale figures, not from the quest text itself.
bugs.where: Reedholm landing (Fenmarch) and the Keepers' Hall (Hollowbrook)

confusions: The realm's true scale relative to any turn budget is stated only once, in small print inside the Act 2 status block, not at the point a player commits to exploring 'the whole hold' in Act 1.

Corliss, one of three named deciders for the Meres' Old Dams quest, has no discoverable location anywhere in the region despite thorough exploration - the quest cannot be seen through to any of its three named outcomes.

Whether the two physical coin-dies I recovered were actually used to strike Pennywell's new coin, or the new press just copied their design while the relics stayed in my pocket, is never resolved by any later text.

The Hunter's Sortie gives no signal whether resolving one of three wolves (with the other two left peacefully alone, at the game's own encouragement) counts as 'done' - the quest simply never updates either way.
The Meres/Pennywell ferry is described as a physical, chained boat but crossing it is indistinguishable from any other footpath tile - there is no moment that reads as 'you take the ferry.'
Travel-menu region groupings don't always match the literal map: a landmark you've stood on (The Far Bank) can be absent from the travel list of the region it actually borders.
suggestions: Mark multi-target quests like The Hunter's Sortie 'done (partial)' once the questgiver accepts the outcome, instead of leaving them open forever.
Either place Corliss somewhere reachable in the Meres or drop her from the Old Dams quest's named cast if she isn't actually placed anywhere.
Give every Warden-flagged entry at least one small consequence (flavor flag, minor xp, or a clear 'this did nothing, try Y instead'), since one I found had zero effect of any kind.
Add a one-line 'you board the ferry' beat at the Meres/Pennywell crossing so the promised ferry reads as an event, not backdrop.
Add a genuine no-roll 'stay out of it' option to companion quarrels, separate from the persuasion-roll 'draw' attempt, so choosing neutrality doesn't itself risk both relationships on a coin flip.
State the turn cost of seeing a hold whole (and the road to the capital) in the opening turns, not only inside the dense Act 2 status paragraph, so players can budget realistically from the start.
Have Sarel, Doran, or Slade reference the two dies by name once Pennywell's bargain resolves, so the carried relics feel spent rather than orphaned in the inventory forever.
Let 'travel to a known place' list every landmark actually visited, regardless of which region category it's filed under.

Fold permanently-unusable sentimental keepsakes out of the default 'carrying:' summary (or into a separate 'keepsakes' line) once they have no further use, so dies/covenant-stone-type items don't get lost in the list.
Attach a rough turn-distance estimate to fetch/report quests offered far from their target hold (e.g. 'this is many turns west'), since the quest text alone gives no sense of scale.

Let the free 'weigh what this grief asks' tool (which was accurate every single time I used it) be discoverable earlier/more prominently, since it's the single best tool in the game for making an informed bargain-vs-rest-vs-burn choice.
